runs.inference: CBMC's all-properties loop only re-solves after sat, so the first answer was very likely sat: at least one check is violable in that encoding. Bitwuzla's answer itself was not captured, and no property or trace was seen. This is not yet a counterexample and says nothing about whether the application or a bound is at fault.
runs.correction_2026_11_03: The inference above is withdrawn. Kani's goto program carries 67 reachability_check probes whose expression is the constant FALSE; a sat from them is expected and reports reachability, not a violation. Run D shows the same formula answering sat on such a probe, so sat here gives no evidence that any real check is violable.

first_real_solver_answer: Bitwuzla answers the unfiltered formula in about 41 to 48 minutes, but that answer is sat on a reachability probe and says nothing about real properties. No solver has yet answered the query over real properties.
sufficiency_of_unwindset: Still unproven. No unwinding assertion has been reported either way.
resume: Do not read VERIFICATION FAILED from direct cbmc without checking the property class; exclude reachability_check as direct4.sh does.
Finding a model took about 41 to 48 minutes even for a trivially reachable probe, so most of the cost may be the formula's memory model and not the query. That is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

Run F (2026-11-03) tried this: real_map_case.assertion.1 alone, 30 VCCs after slicing, no answer in 2700s on a shared VM at load 3-6. A retry is only worth it on an idle VM or with a changed memory model; do not repeat the same run.
Recording a pass still needs every real property unsat on this configuration, plus the wrong-target control.

negative_controls_for_filter.result: On a small C program: filtered with a too-low bound still fails the unwinding assertion; filtered with enough bound succeeds with the probe excluded; unfiltered fails on the probe.
